paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The people in Egypt looked at the ruins of Jerusalem and read them backwards. They said life was good when they burned incense to the Queen of Heaven, and everything fell apart when they stopped (Jeremiah 44:17-18). But Jeremiah tells them the ruins came because of the evil they had done, because they did not obey the voice of the LORD (Jeremiah 44:23).

Now that's a big problem, because you can build a whole life on the wrong explanation. It's like blaming the oven for a burnt batch when you walked off and left the timer ticking. I've done it, friend. Don't ask me how many cookies I've blamed on the oven. The people had the evidence standing in front of them, and they still would not listen, and that's why I take the LORD's warnings seriously. His word is the one that tells the truth about what happened and what's coming.

The LORD says they will all know "whose word will stand, Mine or theirs!" (Jeremiah 44:28). Everything about this passage says His word stands, the warnings and the sign about Pharaoh Hophra alike (Jeremiah 44:29-30). So here's your question to carry out of my bakery: whose word are you building on? I think the safest recipe is the one the LORD wrote, even when the explanation we like better is sitting right there on the counter. And the story isn't over yet, because there's more teaching to come.
